title: The basis of success: relationships
header_line: My analysis of one book on authority and personal brand. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Which single relationship is the root of your business?

I read a statement from the book: the ability to build, sustain and grow relationships is the basis of success and happiness in life, and most of us can trace the roots of our business success to a single relationship. I asked what that means.
I said to take an inventory of the people closest to you: those for a few months, a few years, decades.
A student said: I am strict about how many relationships I allow on my plate at once, because of the attention a relationship needs.
Another said: seasoned business people have little check-in points, such as a birthday in their calendar. It comes down to organization and scheduling.
I said that with long-term relationships, they root for you, and they are interested in where you are going, not only asking what you can do for them.
I said that the author does not do a bait and switch: he builds the relationship, and you lose all credibility when you try to sell or push somebody in a direction.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the relationship that is the root of your work.
Write the people closest to you by time.
Write how many relationships you can really keep.
Write one relationship you have neglected.

check.q: What did a student say seasoned people use?
What did I say you lose by pushing a sale?
What did a student say a relationship needs?

recap: Relationships are the root. Keep them with a schedule.
